name: Sagrada Família
description: Gaudí’s vast basilica, under construction since 1882, with tree-like columns inside and stained glass that fills it with colour.

name: Plaça de Catalunya
description: The big square at the top of La Rambla, where the old city meets the 19th-century Eixample grid.

name: Plaça de Sant Jaume
description: The square at the heart of the Gothic Quarter, where the Catalan government palace and the city hall face each other.

name: Camp Nou
description: FC Barcelona’s home stadium since 1957 and the largest in Europe. It is being rebuilt in stages.

name: Palau de la Música Catalana
places: Palau de la Música Catalana concert hall
description: A modernista concert hall from 1908, covered in mosaics, with a stained-glass skylight over the auditorium.

name: National Art Museum of Catalonia
description: Catalonia’s national art museum, in a palace on Montjuïc built for the 1929 exhibition, known for its Romanesque church murals.

name: Telefónica building
description: The telephone exchange on Plaça de Catalunya that was fought over in the street battles of May 1937, during the Spanish Civil War.

name: Olympic Stadium
description: The stadium on Montjuïc built for the 1929 exhibition and rebuilt as the main stadium of the 1992 Olympics.

name: La Model prison
description: A prison built in 1904 in the Eixample, used to hold political prisoners under Franco. It closed in 2017 and is now open to visitors.

name: Park Güell
description: Gaudí’s hillside park, with mosaic benches, gingerbread-like gatehouses and views over the city.

name: Santa Maria del Mar
description: A 14th-century Gothic church in El Born. The memorial square beside it marks the graves of those killed in the 1714 siege.
